subject: Uptake plan & evaluation-to-commit pathway for TuringAI - GPU pool tiers
messages:
From: Claire Liu <claire@turingai.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Uptake plan & evaluation sprint -> path to commit (TuringAI)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. We want to formalize an evaluation-to-commit pathway so our procurement team can budget. High level: 4-week evaluation sprint, then a commercial decision to commit to a dedicated GPU pool.

Key asks from our side:
- A draft mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to pricing/commit milestones.
- Indicative pricing for dedicated GPU tiers (small/medium/large pools), term options (12/24 months), and any milestone discounts.
- Burst policy: how much headroom for spikes (demos/traffic) and what the overage mechanics are.
- Any SOC2 / encryption notes we should share with procurement.

Can you send a short MAP draft and an indicative commercial outline by EOD Thursday? We want to start the eval on Aug 30.

Thanks — copying Aman (platform lead) who will own the technical acceptance criteria.

—Claire Liu
Head of Platform, TuringAI

ATTACHMENTS: none in this message
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Liu <claire@turingai.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptake plan & evaluation sprint -> path to commit (TuringAI)

Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise evaluation plan (TA-eval-plan-v1.pdf) that maps milestones to decision gates and includes the acceptance criteria Aman can use. Summary highlights below:

Evaluation MAP (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): Access, RBAC, test keys, SOC2 checklist items
- Week 1 (POC): Integration with dev model, latency profiling (baseline target: p95 < 140ms for 512 tokens)
- Week 2 (Integration): KV cache warmup, throughput test at target QPS
- Week 3 (Scale): Ramp test to predicted peak, failure injection
- Week 4 (Decision): Close meeting + commercial handshake or extension

Indicative commercial posture (high-level)
- GPU pool sizing: Small (4x A100-equivalent), Medium (12x), Large (40x) — pricing per GPU-hour attached in pricing-breakdown-commit.csv.
- Term options: 12mo (standard), 24mo (additional 8% discount on committed usage).
- Ramp and milestone discounts: 10% one-time onboarding rebate after successful Integration milestone; additional 5% on invoices after 12-month commit if utilization >= 60%.
- Burst: default allowance is up to 1.5x baseline sustained for up to 48 hours/month free; beyond that overage billed at 1.9x baseline GPU-hour rate. We can flex the free burst for demo windows with a short notice clause.

Open questions for you to confirm: expected steady-state QPS and peak demo QPS (Aman’s numbers will help), and whether you need a canary/fallback model for early rollout.

I’ve attached a SOW stub (SOW-stub-Redwood.docx) for procurement to review. If this looks right I’ll have Ben put together a formal commercial term sheet with explicit SLA language and burst mechanics.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

ATTACHMENTS: TA-eval-plan-v1.pdf; SOW-stub-Redwood.docx
From: Aman Singh <aman.singh@turingai.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Liu <claire@turingai.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptake plan & evaluation sprint -> path to commit (TuringAI)

Jonas — quick clarifications from the platform side:
- Expected steady-state: ~45 concurrent inference QPS, average request ~300 tokens, 99th token rate depends on batch sizing but expect p95 bursts.
- Peak demo spike: up to 180 QPS for short windows (5–10 minutes) during customer demos.
- Security: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and customer-managed KMS for keys in production. The SOC2 statement is fine for the eval; we’ll need KMS integration for the committed environment.

On the burst mechanics: is the 48 hours/month free burst contiguous or aggregated? For our use case it needs to be aggregated to hit multiple demo windows across teams. Also, we’d like a crediting mechanism if Redwood misses the latency SLOs tied to integration milestone (we can accept a service credit vs. a price rebate).

Thanks — Aman
Platform Lead, TuringAI

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Liu <claire@turingai.com>, Aman Singh <aman.singh@turingai.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Commercial outline — TuringAI dedicated capacity (indicative)

Claire / Aman —

Appreciate the detail. Based on your peak and steady-state numbers, here’s an indicative commercial outline and explicit burst mechanics you can share with procurement. This is a non-binding commercial outline; final terms will go into a term sheet.

1) Pricing per GPU-hour (indicative)
- Small pool (4 GPUs): $6.50 / GPU-hour committed rate
- Medium pool (12 GPUs): $5.75 / GPU-hour committed rate
- Large pool (40 GPUs): $4.95 / GPU-hour committed rate

2) Commit & ramp structure
- Minimum commit: 50% of baseline pool for first 3 months, ramp to 100% by month 6 (typical ramp schedule).
- Ramp credits: if Redwood fails to deliver the agreed throughput in months 1–3, we will issue invoice credits up to 20% of those months’ fees.

3) Milestone-linked discounts
- Integration milestone complete: one-time 10% credit applied to next invoice (this is the onboarding rebate Jonas mentioned).
- Signed 24-month term: additional 8% off committed usage for the term.

4) Burst policy (explicit)
- Aggregated free burst: up to 2x committed baseline aggregated across the month for up to 72 hours total. This addresses demo fragmentation.
- Overage beyond free burst: billed at 2.0x the committed GPU-hour rate.
- Emergency demo flex: for scheduled sales events >72 hours, Redwood will make a one-time temporary burst uplift at no charge if notified 48 hours in advance (subject to capacity).

5) SLA & Remedies
- Target p95 latency for agreed model/config: 140ms.
- If Redwood misses the integration milestone SLOs (per MAP acceptance tests), we will offer service credits (not cash refunds) of 5–15% on impacted invoices depending on severity. Credits can be used against future committed usage.

Next steps
- If this is directionally acceptable, we’ll convert to a formal commercial term sheet and schedule an hour with procurement/legal. I’ve attached the pricing CSV for your internal modeling.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
